report:
Reviewed the complete product_availability claim, its single ordinary implementation association in src/inspector.rs, the complete associated TODO test, and the captured review policy. Requirements are positive availability, non-eager selection, opaque IDs plus labels and URLs, identical local/external descriptor mechanism, and absence of unsupported products.

Implementation: selected_symbol resolves a local symbol locator and invokes product_catalog; external_selected_symbol resolves external identity and invokes external_product_catalog. Both return SelectedSymbol.products made from the shared product_descriptor function. That helper copies producer-chosen IDs and labels and formats /api/v1/product URLs with a percent-encoded symbol path; consumers need not derive availability from semantic kinds. The local catalog includes identity for represented symbols, source only when symbol_span exists, and concrete-ir/signature/diagnostics/typed-ir only for local functions. The synthetic crate directory root has no symbol locator and consequently an empty list. The external catalog includes identity, signature only for functions/traits/structs/enums, and items only for modules/enums/traits. Other kind arms do not append those products, and external symbols are not offered local source/body products. These positive cases agree with the dispatch branches in identity_product and external_product; unsupported requests return None rather than supplying unsupported content.

Non-eagerness: catalog construction only branches on symbol kind, local-function identity, and span availability, then builds descriptors. It does not invoke identity_product, external_product, source_product, signature queries, function.body, or reflected-product rendering. Selection may resolve canonical ownership paths and bootstrap the symbol directory; those identity/membership operations are distinct from requesting the selected symbol's advertised products. Canonical external resolution uses owner-child metadata and identity references. Actual signature, source-text, body and diagnostic generation appears behind explicit product requests in the same captured implementation file. Product IDs are producer-defined strings passed through the descriptor mechanism, not an inferred negative capability list.

Tests: the entire associated set is one TODO function, sage_meta::todo::crates_sage_inspector_inspection_product_availability in service_spec.rs. It contains no executable assertions. Its explicit prerequisite is to associate and review complete local/external catalog evidence that asserts exact positive lists and forbids product-detail reads during construction. This is an appropriate visible test deferral for the claim: a future assertion suite must cover descriptor IDs/labels/URLs, local versus external kind matrices, unsupported omissions, and query/request observations during selection. It would catch, for example, eagerly computing a function signature while listing products or advertising typed-ir for an external symbol; the current placeholder would not. Acceptance preserves TODO status and does not claim this coverage exists or that a passing placeholder verifies behavior. No N/A entries or deferred implementation entries exist.

This is source inspection, not test-execution evidence. Executed cargo meta review start and review read; no behavioral tests or builds were run by this reviewer. All implementation logic used for this judgment is in the automatically captured src/inspector.rs; review-policy context was additionally captured through review read. No production, test, or association changes were made. No edits are requested beyond the explicitly represented test-evidence deferral.
